question: change

confidence.reason: We could not compare the new water with another satellite's water map, so this cannot be High.

compared_with_opera: Tonle Sap lake window (103.90-104.12 E, 13.05-13.27 N), Jul to Oct 2026, NISAR track 83: the settings were chosen on this window. Score on the half not used for sweeps: IoU 0.68 [0.64-0.72], precision 0.88, recall 0.75, compared with OPERA new water (docs/accuracy_log.md). This is a comparison with another radar-based map, not validated, and OPERA is not ground truth.
known_failures: cropland plains: IoU 0.04 on one window south of Tonle Sap, 301k px predicted as new water vs 15k in OPERA (docs/GENERALISATION.md)
Sentinel-2 check disagreed on 2 of 2 scored areas: south of Tonle Sap precision 0.15, Kanpur recall 0.03 (docs/accuracy_log.md)

measured.what: all water on the later date (includes permanent river and lake water, so not a test of change)
measured.note: 12 and 24 Sep passes, track 98 A, run with the earlier method version. The two maps disagree: 1,685 ha of ours against 1,879 ha in OPERA, 675 ha shared.

validation.measured_note: Weak: our water and OPERA's overlap on only part of the area.
validation.reference_note: OPERA and Sentinel-2 are other satellite products, not ground truth

limits: These are estimates. Very wet fields can sometimes look like water.
Some spots, like steep hillsides, can't be seen clearly and are left out.
Some NISAR data used is Provisional quality; numbers may change when reprocessed.
Land cover (ESA WorldCover) was not checked, so we cannot say whether new water lies on cropland.
This place and these dates have not been compared with OPERA: the method was compared on one lake window (Jul to Oct 2026, track 83) only.
